best_for: Developers building Android apps on a reasonably recent PC or Mac with at least 16 GB of RAM, who want Google's own tools and emulator.

points.title: Google's IDE for Android
points.text: It is Google's official IDE for Android app development, with Gemini built in for code help. Google offers it as a free download.

points.title: Hungry for RAM and disk
points.text: Google lists 8 GB of RAM for the IDE and 16 GB with the emulator, and recommends 32 GB. You need 8 to 16 GB of free disk, and the emulator needs CPU virtualization turned on.

points.title: Old versions lose cloud features
points.text: Gemini, Crashlytics and other service integrations work only in the latest stable release and major versions from the previous 10 months. An older download still builds apps, without those.

points.title: No Windows on Arm
points.text: Windows needs 64-bit Windows 10 or later on an x64 processor; Arm-based Windows PCs are not supported. Macs get separate Intel and Apple silicon builds.

points.title: The Linux Flatpak is unofficial
points.text: Google ships Linux as a .tar.gz. The Flatpak listed here is a Flathub build that Flathub does not mark as verified, for x64 only.

points.title: Big downloads, or skip the IDE
points.text: Each installer is about 1.5 GB. If you only need the SDK on a build server, the command-line tools are about 160 to 180 MB.

points.title: Older versions on Windows
points.text: The Windows installer installs for the whole machine, and the Windows listing keeps 42 versions. macOS and Linux list only the current release, so downgrades there need another source.
